endorsements.quote: Once the technology has been clinically and legally validated, it must be regulated.
Lastly, providers must be trained in using the resources.
A similar risk assessment tool developed by ONC for the proposed technology would allow a standardized national evaluation of privacy risks.

unlisted_practices: Improve large language models for low-resource languages before using them for medical interpretation.
Have clinician-researchers evaluate AI interpretation accuracy, acceptability across languages, and safety with patient data before clinical use.
Obtain patient consent before AI interpretation technology collects any identifying patient data.
Automatically de-identify patient data collected by AI interpretation tools to mitigate privacy risk in the event of security breaches.
Implement a policy governing patient information accessed and stored by companies building language models for interpretation, similar to HITECH policy for EHRs.
Provide CMS-funded incentives for hospitals that implement AI interpretation services meeting quality metrics.
Have NIH and AHRQ create financial incentives and special emphasis notices for research on AI interpretation.
Have professional societies and physicians promote education through workshops and toolkits on AI interpretation technologies.

screen.reason: This is an editorial discussing the potential, safety, privacy, and regulatory considerations for using large language models for real-time medical translation and interpretation to advance health equity.
